articles.title: Saudi defence pact countries push for peace in Tehran as Houthis launch more attacks
articles.description: By Andrew Mills, Ariba Shahid and Menna AlaaElDinKARACHI/CAIRO, Oct 26 (Reuters) - Top officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday in a bid to de-escalate the Middle East conflict, as Yemen's Houthis launched new attacks on Saudi Arabia and Egypt approved defence support for the Gulf kingdom.The talks were the first high-level contact between Iran and the three nations — which signed the Mecca mutual defence pact in August — since a war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran also spread to Saudi Arabia and Yemen.

articles.title: Iran hosts Saudi defence pact states as Houthis launch more attacks
articles.description: By Andrew Mills, Ariba Shahid and Menna AlaaElDinDOHA/KARACHI/CAIRO, Oct 26 (Reuters) - Top officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan were due in Iran on Monday in a push to de-escalate the regional conflict now afflicting the Gulf kingdom, as Yemen's Houthis launched further attacks on Riyadh's airport and Saudi oil facilities. The talks were the first high-level contact between Iran and the three nations — which signed the Mecca mutual defence pact in August — since a war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran also spread to Saudi Arabia and Yemen.

articles.title: Delegations meeting in Tehran with region on edge over potential for renewed fighting
articles.description: Regional officials say high-level delegations from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey are in Tehran for talks aimed at preventing renewed fighting between Iran and Israel and the United States. Saudi Arabia’s defense minister, Pakistan’s army chief and Turkey’s intelligence chief were meeting with Iranian officials Monday to push for a diplomatic agreement with Washington. The discussions also address Yemen and attacks by Iranian-backed Houthi rebels. The diplomatic effort comes amid escalating threats ahead of Israel’s election Tuesday and the U.S. midterms next week. Iran says diplomacy remains possible but rejects U.S. demands for surrender, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has warned of potential Iranian attacks.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia reopens Riyadh airport terminals as Houthis threaten fresh strikes
articles.description: Saudi Arabia partially reopened Riyadh's King Khalid airport as Houthi rebels threatened further strikes. The move comes amid renewed fighting that has ended a truce largely holding since 2022.

articles.title: Riyadh airport resumes flights following Houthi attacks
articles.description: Riyadh's international airport said flights would resume on Sunday after a two-week closure following strikes from Yemen's Houthis on the Saudi capital, though the Iran-backed group warned of more to come. The Flight Radar monitoring site showed a plane taking off from Riyadh airport early Sunday, heading to the Saudi city of Jeddah. Saudi Arabia, along with Yemen's internationally recognised government that it backs, has faced a wave of Houthi attacks in recent weeks after a years-long truce broke down in the summer.
